{\LARGE\bfseries\sffamily\color{AtlasNavy} Jointly private linear bandits with predictable adversarial contexts\par}\vspace{5pt}
\textbf{Setting ID.} \texttt{ONX\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}JDP\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}ADV\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}CONTEXT}

Online learning and bandits

Each round reveals a context or action-feature set before an action is chosen and its reward with linear mean is observed. The algorithm satisfies joint differential privacy, limiting the influence of one user's information on actions shown to other users. Contexts may depend on the past.

\textbf{Status.} Bounds missing

\textbf{TASK tags.} formulation: Onx jdp adv context; task family: Online bandit

\textbf{MODEL tags.} structure: Linear

\textbf{ORACLE tags.} interface family: Selected reward; operation: Selected reward; public information: Hidden objects explicitly declared; public information: Public inputs explicitly declared

\textbf{ALGORITHMS tags.} adaptivity: Causal protocol; randomization: Private randomness allowed; restriction: Joint differential privacy

\textbf{OUTPUT tags.} certificate: No additional output certificate required; object: Online trajectory

\textbf{METRIC tags.} criterion: Pseudo regret

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}
Each round reveals a context or action-feature set before an action is chosen and its reward with linear mean is observed. The algorithm satisfies joint differential privacy, limiting the influence of one user's information on actions shown to other users. Contexts may depend on the past.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}
A predictable action set \AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal{A}_t\subset\mathbb{R}^d} is revealed each round. Contexts may depend on the past transcript. The parameter \AtlasInlineMath{\theta_\star} is fixed and unknown.


\AtlasMath{\|a\|_2\le L\quad(a\in\mathcal{A}_t),\qquad \|\theta_\star\|_2\le S,\qquad |\langle a,\theta_\star\rangle|\le B.}



\AtlasMath{Y_t=\langle a_t,\theta_\star\rangle+\eta_t,\qquad \mathbb{E}[\eta_t\mid\mathcal{H}_{t-1},a_t]=0.}


Noise is conditionally \AtlasInlineMath{\sigma}-sub-Gaussian given the pre-action history and current action. The privacy sensitivity argument additionally requires realized action-reward pairs to satisfy the following bounds almost surely:


\AtlasMath{\|(a_t,Y_t)\|_2\le\widetilde{L}\qquad\text{almost surely}.}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}
The learner first observes the current context and action set, then selects \AtlasInlineMath{a_t} and receives only that action’s scalar reward. The released action transcript satisfies joint privacy. Rewards for other actions remain hidden.

The parameters \AtlasInlineMath{d,T,L,S,\sigma,B,\widetilde{L},\epsilon_{\mathrm{priv}},\delta_{\mathrm{priv}},\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}} are public. Reward parameters and future information of the admissible environment remain hidden.

Received feedback may be stored and reused in computation. Unrevealed information cannot be requested from past rounds, and consumed random samples cannot receive additional queries. Current-round exceptions are limited to the explicitly supplied full-function access or same-sample two-point interface.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}
The output is the complete action trajectory satisfying feasibility and timing requirements. Randomized mixtures may be implemented before acting. Retrospective averages or convex combinations cannot replace actions that have already incurred loss. No additional optimal value or certificate is required.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}

\AtlasMath{R_T=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left(\max_{a\in\mathcal{A}_t}\langle a,\theta_\star\rangle-\langle a_t,\theta_\star\rangle\right).}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}
The procedure uses \AtlasInlineMath{N=T} reward observations. The source combines linear UCB with a tree mechanism protecting sufficient statistics. Internal matrix and privacy computations do not provide additional free reward queries.

Exploration, initialization, and system identification all consume the stated online budget. Queries, arithmetic, communication rounds or bits, and memory remain joint resources. No arithmetic or bit-complexity optimality is asserted.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}
Neighboring streams \AtlasInlineMath{\mathsf D,\mathsf D^{\prime}} differ only in one user's context/reward pair. The protected output is every action except that user's current recommendation, received privately. For every measurable event \AtlasInlineMath{E}, require:


\AtlasMath{\Pr\!\left(\mathcal{M}(\mathsf D)_{-t}\in E\right)\le e^{\epsilon_{\mathrm{priv}}}\Pr\!\left(\mathcal{M}(\mathsf D^{\prime})_{-t}\in E\right)+\delta_{\mathrm{priv}}.}


The privacy relaxation \AtlasInlineMath{\delta_{\mathrm{priv}}} is distinct from the statistical failure probability \AtlasInlineMath{\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}}.

Causal policies satisfying \AtlasInlineMath{(\epsilon_{\mathrm{priv}},\delta_{\mathrm{priv}})} joint differential privacy are admissible.

Private randomization is allowed, with the seed independent of the fixed instance and future external samples. Internal arithmetic, memory, linear spans, and iteration forms are unrestricted except for the stated computation, communication, privacy, and within-round interaction limits.

The pseudo-regret must obey the bound with probability at least \AtlasInlineMath{1-\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}}, uniformly over contexts, reward distributions, and parameters satisfying the boundedness conditions. Realized observation noise is not included in the regret.

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{2. Notation and parameters}
\AtlasInlineMath{B}: Absolute bound on linear mean reward \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{B\ge0}.

The bound is \AtlasInlineMath{|\langle a,\theta_\star\rangle|\le B}; it does not bound the absolute observed reward Y.

\AtlasInlineMath{L}: Euclidean norm bound on action or feature vectors \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{L>0}.

The condition is \AtlasInlineMath{\|a\|_2\le L}, with the same meaning if actions are denoted x.

\AtlasInlineMath{S}: A Euclidean-norm bound on the hidden linear reward parameter. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{S\ge0}.

The quantity is \AtlasInlineMath{\|\theta_\star\|_2\le S}; it is not a switching budget.

\AtlasInlineMath{T}: Online rounds within the fixed evaluation horizon. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{T\in\mathbb N,\ T\ge1}.

The information protocol fixes feedback count per round. The horizon \AtlasInlineMath{T} is not an independent cumulative scalar-query count.

\AtlasInlineMath{d}: The ambient dimension of actions or feature vectors. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge1}.

Vectors belong to \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb R^d}; dimension is still denoted d when a non-Euclidean norm is used.

\AtlasInlineMath{\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}}: The allowed statistical failure probability. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{0<\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}<1}.

Used only for statistical correctness or high-probability performance, and distinct from the privacy relaxation parameter.

\AtlasInlineMath{\delta_{\mathrm{priv}}}: Additive allowance in approximate differential privacy \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{0\le\delta_{\mathrm{priv}}<1}.

Additive allowance in the output-event probability inequality for adjacent inputs; not statistical confidence.

\AtlasInlineMath{\epsilon_{\mathrm{priv}}}: The multiplicative differential-privacy parameter. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\epsilon_{\mathrm{priv}}>0}.

Use the factor \AtlasInlineMath{e^{\epsilon_{\mathrm{priv}}}} when comparing probabilities of output events under adjacent data inputs.

\AtlasInlineMath{\sigma}: Conditional sub-Gaussian scale of the reward noise \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\sigma\ge0}.

For every \AtlasInlineMath{s\in\mathbb R}, \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb E[e^{s\eta_t}\mid\mathcal H_{t-1},a_t]\le e^{s^2\sigma^2/2}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\widetilde L}: Joint Euclidean norm bound for the actual action and reward \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\widetilde L\ge0}.

The condition \AtlasInlineMath{\|(a_t,Y_t)\|_2\le\widetilde L} holds almost surely and controls the sensitivity of the privacy mechanism.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal A_t}: Predictable action set revealed before acting \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal A_t\subseteq\mathbb R^d}.

Determined by past observations; all actions satisfy the stated norm and mean bounds.

\AtlasInlineMath{\theta_\star,a_t,Y_t,\eta_t}: The hidden parameter, selected action, realized reward, and observation noise. \textbf{Domain:} A quantity in the linear reward model.

Assume \AtlasInlineMath{Y_t=\langle a_t,\theta_\star\rangle+\eta_t} and \AtlasInlineMath{a_t\in\mathcal A_t}; noise has conditional mean zero.

\AtlasInlineMath{\overline B}: The source mean bound, which is at least one. \textbf{Domain:} Positive real number.

\AtlasInlineMath{\overline B=\max\{1,B\}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal M}: The jointly private mechanism releasing recommended actions. \textbf{Domain:} A causal randomized algorithm.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathsf D,\mathsf D^{\prime}}: Adjacent streams differ in one user’s context and reward record. \textbf{Domain:} Adjacent input data streams.

The comparison concerns the full induced distributions of the output action sequence.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal M(\mathsf D)_{-t}}: The output sequence with the current user’s action at position t removed. \textbf{Domain:} Action-sequence random variable.

Joint privacy protects all actions visible to other users. The current recommendation at time \AtlasInlineMath{t} is received privately by that user.

\AtlasInlineMath{E}: A measurable output event in the privacy definition. \textbf{Domain:} Measurable subset of the output space.

The privacy inequality holds for every such event.

\AtlasInlineMath{R_T}: Cumulative pseudoregret evaluated using the mean functions \textbf{Domain:} Nonnegative real-valued random variable.

\AtlasInlineMath{R_T=\sum_t[\max_{a\in\mathcal A_t}\langle a,\theta_\star\rangle-\langle a_t,\theta_\star\rangle]} Realized observation noise is excluded from the loss difference. Probability or expectation aggregation is specified separately by the guarantee.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal A}: Learning policies satisfying the specified information, computation, and privacy restrictions \textbf{Domain:} A measurable causal policy.

Actions may depend only on revealed information and the private seed. Additional restrictions are governed by the algorithm protocol in this profile.

\AtlasInlineMath{t}: Interaction-time index \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{t\in\{1,\ldots,T\}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb E}: Mean operator \textbf{Domain:} Expectation over the specified random variables.

Expectation includes learner randomness and the explicitly specified reward or sample randomness. Conditional expectations retain their stated history conditioning.

\AtlasInlineMath{\log,\log_2}: Natural and binary logarithms \textbf{Domain:} Function on the positive real axis.

\AtlasInlineMath{\log x=\ln x}, \AtlasInlineMath{\log_2x=\log x/\log2}.

\AtlasInlineMath{c,C}: Positive constant in the bound without an assigned numerical value \textbf{Domain:} Positive real number.

Constants apply only under the associated bound’s conditions and fixed-parameter convention. Unspecified theorem constants are not treated as additional algorithm inputs.

\AtlasInlineMath{O,\Omega,\widetilde O,\widetilde\Omega}: Asymptotic upper and lower bounds, including explicitly permitted logarithmic suppression. \textbf{Domain:} Asymptotic comparison notation.

The result applies only in the regime declared for that bound. Tilde notation hides only its stated logarithms and fixed-parameter dependencies, never additional polynomial parameter factors.

\AtlasInlineMath{N}: Cumulative observations counted according to the declared feedback type. \textbf{Domain:} Nonnegative integer or integer-valued stopping time.

The quantity \AtlasInlineMath{N=T} counts cumulative native scalar feedback under a one-point or one-arm protocol.

\textbf{Conditions.} Fixed contract with T>=2, 0<epsilon\_\allowbreak{}priv<=1, 0<delta\_\allowbreak{}priv<1/e and 0<delta\_\allowbreak{}conf<1 (unchanged r1).; Use the frozen bounds ||a||\_\allowbreak{}2<=L, ||theta\_\allowbreak{}star||\_\allowbreak{}2<=S and |<a,theta\_\allowbreak{}star>|<=B.

\textbf{Derivation.} For every feasible action a, |<a,theta\_\allowbreak{}star>|<=||a||\_\allowbreak{}2||theta\_\allowbreak{}star||\_\allowbreak{}2<=LS by Cauchy-Schwarz and the frozen norm bounds. The independent mean bound also gives |<a,theta\_\allowbreak{}star>|<=B. Thus comparator and selected-action means lie in [-min\{B,LS\},min\{B,LS\}]; every nonnegative pseudo-regret summand is <=2 min\{B,LS\}. Summing yields 0<=R\_\allowbreak{}T<=2T min\{B,LS\} pathwise. Apply this inequality to the SAME admissible private strategy retained in b1 on r1: actions, privacy parameters, output and T selected-reward observations are unchanged. If its old event is R\_\allowbreak{}T<=C F with probability >=1-delta\_\allowbreak{}conf, intersection with this probability-one inequality gives R\_\allowbreak{}T<=min\{C F,2T min\{B,LS\}\} at the same confidence, without algorithm selection or union-bound loss. F denotes exactly the explicit rate inside b1's O expression; C is a retained admissible constant. B=0 or S=0 forces exact zero regret by nonnegativity, while the observation budget remains T. The inequality is valid throughout the contract, but native algorithmic adoption here is restricted to r1, using its retained witness. No positive lower bound or matching minimax saturation threshold follows.
